subject.description: EXAMPLE. In a real record this says what was done with the software, in enough detail that a reader can tell whether it is use or a mention. A paper that cites the software in a related-work list is a citation, not use, and the two are different records.

source.value: EXAMPLE: no source exists, because no output exists. A real record carries a DOI, an arXiv id, a handle, or an https URL with an archive snapshot next to it.

verification.note: Nothing was verified. There is nothing to verify: this is a template. A real record names who resolved the identifier and on what date, and the status only becomes "verified" once that has happened.

statusReason: Template only. No institutional use, research output or citation has been recorded for this project, and validation/impact/summary.json counts zero.
notes: EXAMPLE RECORD. It is excluded from every count twice over: as an example, and on a status that is not "verified".

The rule this container enforces is that an impact claim carries a source a stranger can resolve. A record whose only source is our own word is kept at "unverifiable" and never counted; the verifier refuses to let it sit at "verified".
